# Character Motion — killing the "readymade video" feel

Why Mixamo characters read like a played video: discrete pose changes
(Idle→Walk→Run snaps), feet floating over uneven ground, hands hovering near
the gun, a neck that snaps to the aim direction, and a body with no mass when
turning. The fix is **blending + layers + IK + procedural lean**, and this
repository now has all four wired as a runtime motion stack.

## What already existed (generated by `AnimatorControllerBuilder`)

* `Speed`-driven Any-State zone transitions (Idle < 1.5 < Walk < 4.5 < Run
  < 7 < Sprint), no exit time, 0.12 s crossfade;
* a **1D Blend Tree** for crouch locomotion (Crouch ↔ Crouch Walk on `Speed`);
* an **UpperBody layer** (index 1) with a generated AvatarMask
  (`Assets/AvatarMasks/UpperBody.mask`): legs/root disabled, spine/arms/head
  enabled, Override blending — so **shooting while moving already works**:
  RifleIdle/RifleRun play on layer 1 while legs run on layer 0, and
  `PlayerCharacterVisual` damps the layer weight with the aiming state;
* `PlayerCharacterVisual` feeding `Speed` (0.12 s damp), `IsAirborne`,
  `IsCrouching`, `IsAiming`, `Shoot`/`Reload` triggers.

### Why the upright states stay zones instead of one big blend tree

The controller structure is a **test-locked contract**:
`CharacterPipelineTests.BuildController_CreatesAllParametersStatesAndUpperBodyLayer`
and the FBX-repair regression tests assert the exact state names
(`Idle/Walk/Run/Sprint/…`), the single IsAiming Any-State transition and the
UpperBody mask bits — they guard the character repair pipeline. Collapsing
everything into one blend tree would break those guards for a marginal win,
because the "snap" feeling is fixed at runtime instead:

* the zone crossfades are already exit-time-free and 0.12 s;
* **`PlayerLocomotion`** (below) drives `Speed` from *measured displacement*
  with exponential damping, so the parameter itself moves as one continuous
  accel/decel curve — the blend between zones reads seamlessly and the feet
  stop moon-walking.

If you later want a true 1D upright tree, the sanctioned route is
`BlendTreeHelper.CreateBlendTree1D` in the builder **plus** updating the two
protected test files through the repair-manifest flow — not a silent edit.

## The runtime motion stack (`Assets/Scripts/Characters/`)

```
CharacterMotionMath.cs   # pure damping/lean/weight math (EditMode-tested)
PlayerLocomotion.cs      # 1: real CharacterController velocity → Speed param
FootIK.cs                # 3: ground-planting feet (built-in Humanoid IK)
WeaponHandIK.cs          # 3: left hand grips the foregrip point
HeadLookIK.cs            # 5: head follows the camera aim point, eased
ProceduralLean.cs        # 4: spine/chest banking into turns & strafes
CharacterMotionRig.cs    # orchestrator: attaches 1/3/4/5 to the spawned
                         #    character and re-attaches after a bay swap
```

**Wiring**: add one `CharacterMotionRig` to the player root (the GameObject
carrying `PlayerCharacterVisual` + `PlayerController` + `WeaponController`).
It waits for the visual's Animator, then adds the IK/lean components **onto
the Animator's GameObject** (Unity only calls `OnAnimatorIK` on components
sitting there), binds the camera, weapon mount and CharacterController, and
re-attaches automatically when you switch characters in the bay.

### 1. Anti-slide locomotion (the brief's PlayerLocomotion)

`LateUpdate` measures `Δposition/dt` on the XZ plane (after every Update
writer), damps it with `smoothTime ≈ 0.14 s` and writes `Speed`. Standing
still clamps under 0.12 m/s so idle never jitters into the Walk zone.
Vertical motion is excluded — jumping/falling belong to `IsAirborne` +
`VerticalSpeed`.

### 2. Layers (shoot-while-move)

Already generated (see above). The recoil *pose* is deliberately not an
additive layer in the controller — camera-side procedural recoil lives in
`RecoilModel` (docs/gameplay/SHOOTING_MECHANICS.md) and the upper body gets
bracing through `WeaponHandIK` weight (0.5 hip → 0.85 aim). If you want a
true additive recoil layer later: generate a 2–3 frame spine-kick clip, add a
layer with `AnimatorLayerBlendingMode.Additive` + the same UpperBody mask,
and drive its weight from `WeaponController`'s shot event.

### 3. IK — built-in Humanoid first, Animation Rigging for artists

Runtime default is Unity's **built-in Avatar IK** (`OnAnimatorIK` +
`SetIKPosition/Rotation/LookAt`): zero package dependency, zero GC, one code
path on every device. Requirements: the character must be **Humanoid** — the
import gate (`AssetImportRules.IsHumanoidAsset`) already enforces that for
everything under `Assets/Characters` and `UserAssets/Models/{Male,Female}`.

* **FootIK** — per foot: raycast from 0.6 m above the animated foot down
  0.9 m (Terrain + Default layers, own colliders excluded), clamp the goal to
  ±0.3 m of the animated pose, align the sole to the hit normal (70 % blend).
  Weight: 1.0 standing → 0 by 3.5 m/s → 0 airborne. Result: feet plant on the
  quarry rim and compound steps instead of floating/sinking.
* **WeaponHandIK** — left hand to `HandGripTarget` under the WeaponController
  mount (auto-created at `(−0.06, −0.02, 0.22)` local; move it onto your gun
  model's foregrip when real weapon meshes land). Weight 0.5 carry → 0.85 aim.
* **HeadLookIK** — `SetLookAtPosition` at camera + forward × 12 m, weight
  eased 0.35 → 0.9 when aiming, body weight 0.15, smooth 0.4. No neck snaps.

**Animation Rigging (editor route, package pinned in `Packages/manifest.json`
at `com.unity.animation.rigging@1.4.0` — the Unity 6000.0 release; 1.4.3 does
not exist in the registry and broke the APK build until it was repinned)** —
for artists who want tweakable constraints instead of code. If a future Unity
6 patch ever fails to resolve the pin, delete the manifest line and install
Animation Rigging through the Package Manager instead: no runtime code
references the package (the motion stack is built-in Humanoid IK), so builds
never depend on it.

1. Select the character instance root → Add Component → **Rig Builder**.
2. Create a child GameObject "Rig", Add Component → **Rig**; register it in
   the Rig Builder's Layers list (weight 1, active).
3. Two-Bone IK (support hand): under "Rig" add **Two Bone IK Constraint** —
   Root = LeftUpperArm, Mid = LeftLowerArm, Tip = LeftHand; create an empty
   "HandTarget" parented to the weapon mount at the foregrip, assign it as
   the effector Target; Source (Objects) = HandTarget, weight 1.
4. Multi-Aim (head): add **Multi Aim Constraint** — Constrained Object =
   Head bone, a "LookTarget" empty driven by your aim point; enable X/Y/Z
   axes with the head's natural limits, Maintain Aim Offsets on.
5. Bake weights through a small driver script (or Animator parameters via
   Rig constraints' weight bindings) so hip/aim blending matches
   `CharacterMotionMath.HandIkWeight`/`LookWeight`.
6. **Do not run both stacks**: when Rigging constraints own the left hand or
   head, disable `WeaponHandIK`/`HeadLookIK` on that character (the rig
   components no-op when removed/disabled).

### 4. Procedural lean (the brief's ProceduralLean)

`ComputeLeanAnglesDeg(localLateral, yawRate, forwardSpeed)`:

* lateral roll = `clamp(lateralSpeed × 3.5 + yawRate × 0.035, ±8°)` —
  positive leans **right** into right strafes/right turns;
* forward pitch = `clamp01(speed / 7.2) × 6°` while sprinting;
* both damped (0.18 s) and applied as `Quaternion.Slerp`-equivalent local
  rotations, split half on **Spine**, half on **Chest**
  (`Animator.SetBoneLocalRotation` inside `OnAnimatorIK`), so idle breathing
  survives under the lean. Yaw rate is unwrapped across ±180° (tested).

### 5. Tuning table

| Feel problem | Knob | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Moon-walking on stops | `PlayerLocomotion.speedSmoothTime` | 0.14 s |
| Lean too twitchy | `ProceduralLean.leanSmoothTime` | 0.18 s |
| Not enough body in turns | `CharacterMotionMath` lateral gain (3.5) / `maxLateralDeg` | 8° |
| Feet drag while jogging | `FootIkWeight` fade band (0.5→3.5 m/s) | — |
| Neck too robotic at hip | `LookWeight` hip floor | 0.35 |
| Hand floats off foregrip | `WeaponHandIK.defaultGripOffset` | (−0.06,−0.02,0.22) |

All curves are locked by `CharacterMotionTests` (EditMode): damping never
overshoots and is frame-rate independent, lean signs/clamps are exact, IK
weights ramp hip→aim, foot IK zeroes out airborne.

## Performance (UNISOC budget)

Per character per frame: 2 foot raycasts (30 Hz physics step is fine), 4 IK
goal writes, 2 bone local rotations — no allocations, no package runtime
cost when the built-in stack is used. The Animation Rigging route adds its
constraint graph (~0.05–0.15 ms/character on mid-range); keep Rigging for the
main character only, never for background bots — bots use the built-in stack
or nothing.
